children: Peru’s trade surplus widened to USD 3,309 million in July 2026 from USD 2,432 million in the same month a year earlier.
Exports surged 33.4% year-on-year to USD 10,068 million, driven by higher sales of traditional products (43.6%) and non-traditional products (4.5%), while other products fell 3.4%.
Meanwhile, imports grew 32.2% to USD 6,759 million, led by increases in consumer goods (37.1%), supplies (29.0%), and capital goods (43.5%), while imports of other goods plunged 95.9%.
Over the first seven months of the year, Peru recorded a trade surplus of USD 26,064 million, expanding sharply from USD 15,738 million in the same period last year.
Exports totaled USD 66,506 million, 36.9% higher than a year earlier, while imports amounted to USD 40,441 million, an increase of 23.2%.

title: Peru Trade Surplus Widens in July
